runtime.name: codex-cli
runtime.configuration: Persisted sessions in a disposable isolated Codex state directory with user config and rules ignored; generated Skill linked under project .agents/skills.
runtime.permissionProfile: read-only sandbox with approval policy never

assertions.evidence: The parent read the generated check-cancellation Skill before executing it.
The parent transcript recorded a spawn_agent call and started child thread generation_1.
interrupt_agent targeted generation_1 and returned previous_status=running.
The parent recorded an interrupted activity for the same generation_1 child thread.
The generation_2 spawn appears after the generation_1 interruption acknowledgement in the parent transcript.
Generation 2 alone returned FRESH_MARKER=fresh-ok, which the parent reported as ACCEPTED_MARKER=fresh-ok.
The final report states GENERATION_1_STALE=true, STALE_RESULT_ACCEPTED=false, and STALE_OUTPUT_RECEIVED=false.
The final agent snapshot reports generation_1 interrupted and generation_2 completed.
The parent re-read assets/root.txt after generation 2 completed and observed ROOT_MARKER=cancellation-root-ok.
All threads inherited the read-only sandbox and the external post-run Git status was clean.

limitations: Generation 1 was interrupted before it produced a stale payload, so the accepted-result policy is proven for an interrupted active generation but not for a cancellation race that delivers a late payload.
This W3-targeted fixture proves native cancellation and stale-generation exclusion only; writer isolation, panels, and transcript API access remain unproven, so workflowAchieved remains W2.
The top-level JSON stream omits spawn and interrupt detail; persisted isolated transcripts are the authoritative lifecycle evidence.
Codex CLI lifecycle probes require persisted sessions; this evidence does not apply to ephemeral mode, desktop, or IDE surfaces.
